title: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5
gist: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5, its cheapest and fastest model, priced 90% below Haiku 4.5 for prompts up to 100k tokens (~75% cheaper per task on average) while posting large benchmark gains (e.g., OSWorld 72.4% vs 15.7%). It is pitched as a high-volume subagent under Opus/Sonnet 5.5 rather than a replacement for complex agentic coding, alongside a 50% Sonnet 5.5 cache-read cut (~20% cheaper agentic work) and new monthly API credits for Max and Team subscribers.

insights.claim: Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 costs around 75% less to run on average than Haiku 4.5, after accounting for its new tokenizer using slightly more tokens per task.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Per-task cost of small-model inference is falling by multiples within a single model generation, compressing pricing for the whole low-end LLM tier.
insights.quote: On average, it now costs around 75% less to run.

insights.claim: Haiku 5.5 list pricing is $0.10/$0.50 per million input/output tokens for prompts up to 100k tokens (vs $1.00/$5.00 for Haiku 4.5) — a 90% cut — and $0.50/$2.50 above 100k tokens, a 50% cut; cache reads fall to $0.01 per million.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Tiered long-context pricing steers volume toward short prompts while still undercutting the predecessor on long ones; a 10x price cut on the bulk tier reprices high-volume workloads.

insights.claim: About 90% of requests to Haiku 4.5 used prompts of 100,000 tokens or fewer, which is why Anthropic designed Haiku 5.5's pricing to be cheapest in that band.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Reveals real-world small-model usage is dominated by short-context calls — pricing aimed at that band captures most of the volume.
insights.quote: which make up around 90% of requests to our previous Haiku model

insights.claim: Haiku 5.5 is positioned to unlock narrowly scoped tasks — compaction, summarization, subagent work — that were previously cost-prohibitive with earlier Claude models.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Price elasticity: lower unit cost expands addressable workloads, implying token volume growth may outpace revenue-per-token decline.
insights.quote: tasks that might otherwise have been cost-prohibitive with previous versions of Claude
insights.locator: This chart illustrates an important difference

insights.claim: Anthropic frames Haiku 5.5 as a subagent paired with Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 on coding work, handling high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks like summaries, compactions, database queries and classification.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Agent architectures are converging on an orchestrator/subagent split, where cheap fast models do the bulk of token-heavy grunt work under a frontier lead.
insights.quote: It pairs well with Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 as a subagent on coding work.

insights.claim: Anthropic explicitly concedes that Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 remain the better choice for complex agentic coding; Haiku 5.5 scores 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 70.6% for Sonnet 5.5.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: The small model is not a substitute for frontier models on hard agentic work, protecting premium-tier demand from cannibalization.
insights.quote: Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 remain better choices for complex agentic coding tasks
insights.locator: This chart illustrates an important difference

insights.claim: Cognition reports that using Haiku 5.5 as the 'sidekick' to Opus 5.5 in Devin Fusion holds a top-tier FrontierCode score of 66.2 while cutting cost and latency.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Mixed-model agent stacks can preserve frontier-level coding quality at lower cost — a lever for margin at AI coding companies.
insights.quote: Fusion holds a top-tier FrontierCode score of 66.2 while cutting cost and latency
insights.locator: Claude Haiku 5.5 joins the sidekick lineup

insights.claim: Rogo uses a Haiku 5.5 subagent to pull specific line items such as segment revenue from 10-Ks while a bigger model builds the deck, citing it as accurate enough to trust and cheap enough to run frequently.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Financial-services AI workflows are being decomposed into many cheap retrieval calls, increasing call volume per user task.
insights.quote: a Haiku 5.5 subagent goes into the 10-K and pulls the segment revenue line the deck needs

insights.claim: Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku-class model with an adjustable effort setting (Low to Max), letting users trade cost against intelligence as with larger Claude models.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Effort dials blur model-tier boundaries: buyers can tune cost/quality within one model, complicating simple per-token price comparisons.
insights.quote: Haiku 5.5 is our first Haiku-class model to come with an adjustable effort setting.

insights.claim: On Anthropic's reported benchmarks Haiku 5.5 dramatically outperforms Haiku 4.5: OSWorld 2.1 offline subset 72.4% vs 15.7%, Terminal-Bench 4.0 39.2% vs 0.0%, Humanity's Last Exam (no tools) 45.9% vs 10.2%, and Chartography 46.4% vs 6.4%.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: A generational jump this large in the small tier means capabilities that were frontier-only recently are becoming commodity-priced.

insights.claim: Haiku 5.5 beats OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna on most listed benchmarks, e.g. OSWorld 2.1 offline 72.4% vs 48.9%, Terminal-Bench 4.0 39.2% vs 16.4%, and FrontierCode 1.1 46.4% vs 42.4%.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Small-model competition between Anthropic and OpenAI is intensifying on agentic/computer-use tasks, pressuring price and capability at the low end. Figures are vendor-reported.

insights.claim: Asana saw over a 30% reduction in task-completion latency and up to 2.5x faster inference per agent turn with Haiku 5.5 versus its current model in its AI Teammates product.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Latency gains matter for interactive agent UX and can shift enterprise model selection toward the new small model.
insights.quote: we saw over a 30% reduction in latency for task completions and up to 2.5x faster inference per agent turn
insights.locator: We’re very impressed with Claude Haiku 5.5

insights.claim: HubSpot reports Haiku 5.5 achieved the best score it has seen on its CRM evaluation suite of smaller models, 92.8% averaged over three runs, and was fastest with the highest hit rate and lowest false-positive rate on a CRM audit task.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Small models are becoming good enough for structured enterprise CRM tasks, lowering the cost of embedding AI in SaaS.
insights.quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 got the best score we’ve seen on this suite yet, at 92.8% averaged over three runs
insights.locator: At HubSpot, we use simulated portals

insights.claim: AlphaSense's 'Ask in Document' feature runs about 8M calls a week and is one of its biggest spend lines; on 400 queries Haiku 5.5 scored 0.84 vs 0.76 for Haiku 4.5, a statistically significant improvement.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: High-volume enterprise AI features are major cost centers, so a cheaper and better small model directly improves software-vendor gross margins.
insights.quote: doing about 8M calls a week in production
insights.locator: Ask in Document is one of

insights.claim: Box reports Haiku 5.5 scored 11 points higher than Haiku 4.5 at about half the latency in early testing, and plans to use it for analytical work at scale such as cost reports and financial summaries.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Enterprise content platforms are actively optimizing model choice for cost at scale, favoring cheap capable small models.
insights.quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 scored 11 points higher than Haiku 4.5 at about half the latency

insights.claim: Anthropic is halving Sonnet 5.5 cache-read prices from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens; because cache reads are a large share of token consumption, this cuts Sonnet 5.5's cost on most agentic tasks by around 20%.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Cache reads dominate agentic token mix, so cache pricing is now a key competitive lever — headline input/output prices understate real agent costs.
insights.quote: Because cache reads make up a large share of models’ token consumption, this reduces the cost of Sonnet 5.5 on most agentic tasks by around 20%.

insights.claim: Anthropic is introducing monthly API credits for subscribers — $100 for Max 5x, $200 for Max 20x, and up to $500 pooled for Team — usable on any model to encourage building agents and apps on the Claude Platform.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Bundling API credits into consumer/team subscriptions is a funnel to convert chat subscribers into API developers, deepening platform lock-in.

insights.claim: Anthropic is adding beta computer-use and browser-use support to its Python and TypeScript SDKs, and says Haiku 5.5's speed-capability-price mix makes it especially suited to these tasks.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Cheap, fast models plus SDK support could make browser/computer-use agents economically viable at scale, expanding agent workloads.
insights.quote: Haiku 5.5 is especially well-suited to these tasks, given its combination of speed, capability, and price.

insights.claim: Haiku 5.5 is available on all major clouds — AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure — as well as the Claude Platform at launch.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Multi-cloud distribution at launch reinforces Anthropic's hyperscaler-neutral positioning and broadens enterprise reach.
insights.quote: available now on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure

insights.claim: Haiku 5.5's cybersecurity safeguards are more restrictive than Haiku 4.5's but less restrictive than other recent Anthropic models, permitting more defensive tasks than Sonnet 5.5 while still blocking penetration testing.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Anthropic is tiering safeguards by model capability, with verification programs (Life Sciences, Cyber) gating wider access — a template for capability-scaled access control.
insights.quote: they still block penetration testing and other techniques more likely to be used by attackers

insights.claim: Anthropic says Haiku 5.5 shows major improvements on almost all its alignment evaluations versus Haiku 4.5, with far fewer misaligned behaviors and lower willingness to cooperate with misuse.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Safety improvements in cheap high-volume models matter because they will be deployed at the largest scale with the least oversight.
insights.quote: we found far fewer instances of misaligned behavior, and a lower willingness to cooperate with misuse
